6 bytes, or 48 bits, for each of the destination and source addresses.
0x0800 is IPv4, 0x86DD is IPv6, 0x0806 is ARP.
1500 bytes of data. With the header and FCS, the frame is 1518 bytes.
6 + 6 + 2 + 46 + 4 = 64 bytes. Shorter data is padded up to 46 bytes.
Header (destination, source, EtherType) in front, data in the middle, the 4-byte FCS last.
The data field must be at least 46 bytes: 46 - 30 = 16 bytes of padding.
Undersized frames are usually the leftovers of a collision, so receivers drop them.
64 + 8 + 12 = 84. The frame itself is still 64 bytes.
A switch or router that only takes 1500-byte frames will drop the bigger ones.
